items.title: 'Evil inside him': Dezi Freeman's nephew speaks out on cop killer uncle's death
items.description: When Dezi Freeman was shot dead it left his family with mixed emotions. Some are shattered, others know an "evil man" is dead. His nephew speaks out.

items.title: 'It's going to be painful every year': Zomi Frankcom's family call for answers
items.description: Two years ago on Wednesday, 1 April, Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom was killed by an IDF strike in Gaza. Her family still want answers and accountability.

items.title: RBA to remove surcharges on debit, credit cards and card networks
items.description: The removal of surcharges on debit and credit cards is one of the sweeping reforms from the Reserve Bank.

items.title: Disability agency adds nearly 2,000 new jobs as it seeks to rein in costs
items.description: The agency that runs the National Disability Insurance Scheme defends hiring nearly 2,000 new employees last year despite major changes being rolled out to rein in the program's cost.

items.title: Live: Israel's ground invasion of Lebanon is '100pc defensive', ambassador says
items.description: Israel's ambassador to Australia says the incursion of ground troops into southern Lebanon is "100 per cent defensive" as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says the country is "beyond the halfway point" in achieving its Iran war goals. Follow live.

items.title: Man accused of failed Invasion Day rally bomb may enter insanity plea
items.description: A man accused of tossing a homemade "fragment bomb" filled with ball bearings and screws into a crowd in Perth's CBD flags through his lawyer that he may argue he is not criminally responsible for his actions due to insanity.

items.title: Live: Socceroos roar to life with quick goals against Curaçao in World Cup farewell
items.description: Curaçao is giving the Socceroos a major fight, the sides locked at 1-1 in the Australians' World Cup farewell match. Follow live.

items.title: Australia has not yet reached 'tipping point' for WFH directive, says expert
items.description: The fuel crisis is putting pressure on workers who rely on car travel and those who meet with vulnerable clients, with fresh calls for frontline support staff to be exempt from any future fuel rationing mandates.

items.title: Thousands of Chinese social media users change profile photos to Kris Jenner
items.description: Thousands of Chinese social media users have started using images of US celebrity Kris Jenner as their profile photos in hopes it will bring them success and good fortune.

items.title: Why the 'ultimate' Barbie fan event left visitors wanting a refund
items.description: Barbie fans who paid up to $656 for an "unforgettable experience" were met with a concrete-floored warehouse and flimsy pink cardboard cut-outs.

items.title: Prized WA tourism hotspots forced to close to holiday-makers for Easter
items.description: Famed holiday hotspots in Western Australia's north, including Exmouth and Coral Bay, are reluctantly turning away tourists ahead of the Easter holiday peak as they rebuild in the wake of Cyclone Narelle.

items.title: Fair Work Commission abolishes junior pay rates for young adults
items.description: The Fair Work Commission has issued its decision to abolish junior pay rates for young adult employees in the retail, fast food, and pharmacy sectors while maintaining them for minors.

items.title: ABC proposes new pay offer to staff after 24-hour strike
items.description: The updated ABC offer includes new provisions to ensure staff progress through pay bandings.

items.title: Tim Rogers is an Aussie rock legend — that doesn't impress the bank
items.description: The frontman of ARIA Hall Of Famers You Am I on work, family, and why Hourly, Daily is still special to him.

items.title: 'Why isn't it happening for me?' Three women on being perpetually single
items.description: Three women share their experiences of never having a partner — not by choice — and what that's like when you wish you did.

items.title: Transphobia nearly killed Kaz. Now he just wants to be 'me'
items.description: This WA teenager was depressed, ill and missing out on school. He says it was part of the toll transphobia took on him.

items.title: Boaties find themselves in stand-off with stowaway sugar glider
items.description: The nocturnal marsupial, which typically spends the day sleeping in tree hollows, was discovered when the sails of the boat were opened.

items.title: Report card issued on Antarctic division's cultural reforms
items.description: Workplace reforms implemented by the Australian Antarctic Division (AAD) after two damning reports into the organisation's culture have led to some improvements but a review has found problems persist.

items.title: Jackie O claiming 'at least' $82m in legal action against ARN Media
items.description: Former Sydney radio broadcaster Jackie "O" Henderson has filed legal action against employer ARN Media, following the collapse of the hit Kyle and Jackie O Show.

items.title: IOC's proposed gender test not fit for purpose, says man who discovered it
items.description: The scientist who discovered the SRY gene test that the International Olympic Committee is now relying on to determine athletes' eligibility for women's events says it should not be used in such a fashion.

items.title: Melbourne couple allegedly beat and starved woman enslaved in their home
items.description: A court has heard an Indonesian woman was allegedly threatened and coerced to provide domestic services while living with a Melbourne couple.

items.title: Hundreds gather to farewell 'Welcome to Country' pioneer
items.description: Rhoda Roberts AO is being remembered for her ability to laugh and embrace life, as well as her contribution to the Australian arts and Indigenous cultural movements.

items.title: Vaping likely to cause cancer, new Australian review of evidence finds
items.description: Nicotine-based vapes are likely to cause lung and oral cancer, according to a new review of evidence. Experts say there needs to be tougher enforcement of vape laws in Australia.

items.title: 'I'm sick of it': One in two Australians priced out of healthcare system
items.description: One in two Australians missed out on health care they needed last year mainly because they could not afford it, according to a new report by the peak healthcare consumers group.

items.title: The 10 pivotal events that led to the downfall of Essendon and Carlton
items.description: Essendon and Carlton were once mainstays when it came to the business end of the AFL season. Over the last quarter century, both clubs have fallen on hard times. Here's why.
